ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within $\triangle ABC$, G is any point on side BC, and D, E, and F are the midpoints of AG, BD, and CE respectively. If the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $48$, then what is the value of the area of $\triangle DEF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Draw the line CD as shown in the figure: \\
$\because$ Point D is the midpoint of AG,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle ABD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\triangle ABG}$, $S_{\triangle ACD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\triangle AGC}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle ABD}+S_{\triangle ACD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\triangle ABC}=24$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\triangle ABC}=24$,\\
$\because$ Point E is the midpoint of BD,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle CDE}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\triangle BCD}=12$,\\
$\because$ Point F is the midpoint of CE,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle DEF}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\triangle CDE}=\boxed{6}$.
